did_you_know.text: Did you know? Only after Solomon had completed building the house of the Lord, the royal palace, and all the construction projects he desired did the Lord appear to him a second time.
Did you know? The Lord said that he had consecrated the temple for his name, and that his eyes and heart would be there continually—but this promise was conditional on faithfulness.
Did you know? The continuation of Solomon’s dynasty on the throne depended on walking in the ways of David and keeping the Lord’s laws and ordinances.
Did you know? The chapter warns that idolatry could lead to Israel’s exile, the destruction of the temple, and the nations’ astonishment at its punishment.
Did you know? At the end of twenty years of building—the house of the Lord and the royal palace—Solomon gave Hiram king of Tyre twenty cities in the land of Galilee.
Did you know? Hiram was not pleased with the cities he received, so he called the region the Land of Cabul; nevertheless, he sent Solomon one hundred and twenty talents of gold.
Did you know? The forced labor Solomon imposed was for building the house of the Lord, the royal palace, the Millo, the wall of Jerusalem, and fortified cities such as Hazor, Megiddo, and Gezer.
Did you know? Gezer had been captured and burned by Pharaoh king of Egypt, who gave it as a wedding gift to his daughter, Solomon’s wife; afterward, Solomon rebuilt it.

Did you know? The chapter distinguishes between the foreigners who remained in the land and were conscripted for forced labor, and the Israelites, who served as soldiers, officials, commanders, and army officers.
Did you know? Solomon’s fleet of ships, built at Ezion-geber with the help of Hiram’s sailors, brought four hundred and twenty talents of gold from Ophir.
